title: POC Weekly Sync - App Integration: SDK + Tool/Function Calls + Structured Output
summary: Weekly POC sync reviewing SDK integration progress, structured output schema enforcement, function/tool calling behavior, latency/cost tuning, and next steps for pilot validation. Agreed to run app-level benchmarks and follow up on security docs and a small canonical prompt set for quality checks.
topics: pilot success criteria and next steps
next_steps: Redwood: send updated sample SDK snippets and small benchmark script (Priya)
LumenPay: provide canonical prompt set + 10 real examples for structured output validation (Aisha)

Schedule 1-hour latency benchmark run next Tue and share results (both teams)
Agree on success metrics and finalize pilot end date (Pilot ends 2027-01-31 unless extended)

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-21 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (LumenPay CTO), Aisha Khan (Lead Eng), Tom Briggs (Product), Mei Park (Data/ML), Samir Das (Infra)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is our weekly POC sync with LumenPay. quick agenda, SDK integration status, function/tool calling behavior, structured output validation, and latency/cost tuning. priya you wanna kick off with the SDK bits?

[00:18] Priya: yeah sure, thanks jordan. so from our side we pushed the latest SDK example that uses the app-integration helper, so the call flow is sampleRequest -> Redwood SDK -> model (we're using redwood-api v2 dev endpoint) -> function hooks for payment_verification and account_lookup. there was one minor bug where the SDK retry logic retried on 4xx, um that got fixed this morning.

[00:38] Aisha: cool, i pulled the snippet. quick question, does the SDK currently support streaming + function calls? we need to stream partial responses to the UI while also invoking tools.

[00:51] Priya: good q. streaming with tool calls is supported but caveat — when a function call is triggered we buffer until the function payload completes, so you might see a short hold. That behavior is by design to keep deterministic JSON output. We can make it more optimistic if you prefer partial stream then function result patch-in.

[01:12] Tom: hmm product-wise i think short hold is fine as long as the UI shows progress. our users care more about correctness for payment confirmations than mid-utterance tokens.

[01:24] Carlos: one thing from infra — our legal/security team is picky about payloads leaving the VPC. are these function payloads going to Redwood-hosted tools or our private endpoints?

[01:36] Jordan: great point. right now in the POC we have two patterns: 1) Redwood-hosted tool adapter for quick prototyping (not used for sensitive data), 2) Customer-controlled webhook (your private endpoint) which the SDK calls via VPC peering or private link. Samir, you wanted to confirm peering windows?

[01:50] Samir: yes we tracked the peering request, i put a note to open the peering during the benchmark window 12/28-12/29. i need the ip ranges and ports.

[02:02] Priya: i'll put the ip ranges in the doc and include sample nginx rules. also note: if you prefer Redwood Private, that'd remove egress concerns. but that adds setup time.

[02:16] Mei: on the ML side, we ran some structured-output checks. with your current schema (payment_confirmation {status, txn_id, amount, meta}), about 92% of outputs matched strict JSON schema without post-processing when we used the curated prompt templates. the failures are mostly optional fields out-of-order or stray filler tokens.

[02:34] Aisha: 92% is promising. which model and quantization profile was that on?

[02:40] Mei: it was running on rwinf-3b-v1-q4 (your test dev host) at 64 token context windows, batching 8. We saw deviations when we've got longer customer phrases, like longaddresses or special unicode.

[02:53] Priya: for the structured output enforcement we recommend two approaches: 1) function-calling style where the model emits a single function call with args as JSON (strongly typed), 2) schema-constrained generation with a JSON schema validator + soft prompts. function-calling is more reliable but requires you to implement the function handler.

[03:12] Tom: okay function-calling sounds good. what about nested objects? our txn.meta can include arrays and nested metadata. any issues?

[03:20] Priya: nested is fine, but complexity increases failure modes. For example the model sometimes abbreviates keys or drops nulls. Mei suggested canonicalization step post-model to enforce keys and types. we can share a small library that does schema filling and field normalization.

[03:36] Aisha: would prefer the library. less glue for product.

[03:41] Jordan: we'll attach that library to the repo. Priya: add to action items.

[03:46] [04:02] Mei: on the quality front we noticed two categories of failure in the 8%: structural errors (missing commas, stray text outside JSON) and semantic mismatches (wrong currency code, swapped amount/fee). the structural errors dropped to ~1.5% when we enforced function calls. semantic errors still need prompt engineering.

[04:20] Carlos: semantic errors are the biggest risk for us. a wrong amount is bad. can you run a quick ablation between streaming + non-streaming? maybe buffering changes semantics?

[04:33] Priya: streaming shouldn't change semantics significantly; it's more about when the model truncates due to tokens. we recommend increasing response token budget or using cache/prefix tokens for common instructions. Also using a separate verification function that re-checks output fields against rules reduces risk — e.g., verify_amount(txn.amount) against ledger.

[04:52] Samir: verification function sounds like the right pattern for production. we can host verification inside our infra (customer webhook) so no sensitive payloads leave environment.

[05:03] Jordan: good. switching to performance, Mei can you summarise the latency numbers from last week's run?

[05:09] Mei: sure. end-to-end median after SDK overhead was 310ms for small lookups (<=50 tokens) and 760ms for full confirmations (~220 tokens). p95 was 920ms and 1.8s respectively. these are on the dev host with batching 4-8 and q4 quant. cost per 1k tokens estimate is inline with our earlier spreadsheet.

[05:30] Aisha: 760ms median for our full flow is a bit higher than our goal (target 500ms). any tuning we can do on batching or kernel selection?

[05:39] Priya: yeah two knobs: reduce batching to favor latency (batch 1-2) which raises per-token cost, or quantization profile changes (q3) that reduce latency slightly but need validation for accuracy. also prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts helps. if you have many repeated patterns (like the same account lookup), cache cut median by ~120ms.

[05:59] Tom: what's the unit cost delta if we lower batch size?

[06:05] Mei: rough numbers: batch 8 -> $0.65 per 1k tokens, batch 2 -> $1.10 per 1k tokens. depends on token mix.

[06:13] Carlos: for pilot we can accept higher cost if latency meets product SLAs.

[06:18] Jordan: agreed. proposal: run two benchmark runs next Tue — one optimized for latency (batch 1-2, q3) and one optimized for cost (batch 8, q4) and compare quality on canonical prompts. Priya will provide run script.

[06:33] Priya: i'll include parameters and a smoke test harness. also note we have an internal tool to capture per-route token breakdowns, will share a sample dashboard link.

[06:43] Aisha: also want example SDK code for function handlers in Node and Go. our stack is Go on backend.

[06:50] Priya: we have both; i'll push go examples to the repo. they include signature verification and sample local mocks.

[06:58] Samir: on security, can you confirm where logs live and retention? legal asked about PII retention and audit logs.

[07:06] Jordan: logs for hosted calls are retained per the pilot agreement; we'll send the security packet. we have options: redact PII at ingestion, or disable retention and route logs to your splunk via syslog for the POC. I'll attach SOC2 report.

[07:20] Carlos: please do. also need RBAC for team members so only certain folks can read raw transcripts.

[07:26] Jordan: RBAC supported in console; will share a sample role mapping.

[07:32] Mei: one more ML note: for structured output validation we recommend adding a short verification pass (prompted) that asks the model to "validate" its JSON and output a boolean + errors field; this is cheaper than a whole second model call because you can do it with short prompt and lower token budget. it caught ~60% of semantic mismatches in our tests.

[07:50] Aisha: nice, add that to the runbook.

[07:54] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps and owners. Priya to deliver benchmark script and ip ranges; Jordan to send security docs and role mapping; Aisha to provide canonical prompts and examples; Samir to confirm peering windows; Mei to run baseline quality report and include the validate-pass experiment. everyone agree?

[08:12] Carlos: yes. timeline ok — we expect bench next Tue and results Wed.

[08:18] Tom: one ask — can you include a short demo video of SDK flow in the repo for product folks?

[08:24] Priya: yes we can record a 4-5 minute screencast and link it.

[08:28] Jordan: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links (bench script, security pack, go/node handler snippets). meeting adjourned.

End of transcript
